output.subject: We've received your complaint about your mortgage forbearance
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us. We're sorry for the stress and frustration this has caused, especially at an already difficult time after being laid off.

We have received your complaint. You told us that in May you were approved for a three-month forbearance on your mortgage, and that you have an approval letter dated May 31. You mentioned that you are now receiving letters saying you are past due by $5,862.30, along with collection calls two or three times a day. You also told us that this week you learned you had been reported late to the credit bureaus for July and August, and that you did everything you were asked to do.

You've asked us to fix this, including the past-due letters, the collection calls, and the late payments reported to the credit bureaus.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days.

Thank you for your patience while we look into this.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Verify the forbearance approval dated May 31: its terms, start date, and whether it was applied to the loan.
Confirm whether the July and August credit bureau reporting was accurate and decide on any correction.
Check whether collection calls and past-due letters were sent during the forbearance period and whether they should be paused.
Review the $5,862.30 past-due amount against the forbearance terms.
Decide whether to ask the customer for a copy of the approval letter.
Customer is recently unemployed; consider whether hardship or vulnerability support applies.
The complaint raises potential regulatory exposure (servicing during forbearance, credit reporting); route per policy before any substantive reply.
